newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse down ahead of Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse down ahead of Fed meeting.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade on Monday down nearly one percent, slipping on profit-taking after recent sharp gains and ongoing uncertainity ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 19.06 points at 2,627.04, or a loss of 0.72 percent for the session.
The DAX was under pressure ahead of the U.S. central bank meeting and speculation that they will raise U.S. rates. Some traders said the market had already factored in a small increase in U.S. rates.
"People are holding off ahead of the Fed and are generally unwilling to buy at these levels," said one trader, referring to the record highs reached by German shares in recent days.
Dollar-sensitive chemical shares were unable to buck the downward trend despite a firm dollar, with Hoechst AG falling 34 pfennigs to 54.91 marks and BASF down 60 pfennigs at 47.18 marks.
Insurance group Munich Re held up fairly well on its DAX 30 debut given the market conditions, falling just three marks to 3,447.00 marks.
Linotype-Hell AG ended up seven marks at 130 marks after Linotype chief executive said he would quit. He will be replaced by an executive from Linotype's new owner, Heidelberger Druck.
